biography.plain_text: Lang Walker was an Australian property developer who co-founded the business that became Walker Corporation with his father. He expanded from earthmoving into residential, commercial and industrial development, sold substantial parts of the enterprise twice, and rebuilt it. His later projects included major urban precincts in Sydney, Melbourne and Adelaide.

long_biography.plain_text:
Australian developer Lang Walker brought his negotiating experience to the creation of Chris O'Brien Lifehouse, a cancer hospital in Sydney. A conversation with surgeon Chris O'Brien at a wedding prompted his involvement. He helped reduce construction costs and supported completion of the hospital within two years.

His contribution continued after the building opened. A personal donation helped the hospital acquire a surgical robot for minimally invasive procedures. The Walker Family Foundation subsequently endowed a professorial chair in head and neck cancer reconstruction, supporting the development of a laboratory that combined surgical research with prosthetics. The laboratory opened after his death.
